contract:
# Contract: the session diagram (animated orchestration flow)

You are working in a git worktree for an orchestrator who reviews, refactors and commits your
work. Work here, not in the main checkout. Leave changes uncommitted and do not push.
Ask through `ask_orchestrator` only when blocked by something the contract and repo do not
settle, or when a decision with real consequences is needed. Those calls pause your work.
Progress reports, findings and corrections go in the hand-off, not in questions.

## Context for every unit

`site/` is foreman's landing page (Astro 7 static, React islands, Tailwind 4, Bun), at
https://foreman.steamfield.io. Four delegates build its sections in parallel from the same
commit, each owning different files. The orchestrator designed the page and owns the layout,
the tokens and `src/pages/index.astro`, which already renders your component through the
stub interface in your scope. Keep that interface's export names and props unless the
contract says otherwise; you may enrich the types it names.

Read first, in `site/`: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/PRODUCT.md` (the spec: your section's question and
outline entry), `DESIGN.md` (all of it: tokens, the rule about orange, type, shape, motion,
accessibility), `src/styles/global.css` (token utility names), `src/components/landing/primitives.tsx`
(reuse `Section`, `DataTable`, `CodeFrame`, `StateBadge`, `Inline`; don't fork them),
`src/data/runs.ts` (the recorded-run types), `src/lib/format.ts`, `src/data/landing.ts` (copy),
and `src/pages/index.astro` (where your component sits). Look at one recording in
`fixtures/runs/` and `fixtures/cli/`.

Rules that apply to every unit:

- Demos replay recordings. Never hand-write foreman output or Codex events: take them from
  `fixtures/`. Prose written for the page (Claude's side of a conversation, captions) is
  labeled as written for the page where it appears beside recorded output.
- Style with the token utilities from `global.css` (`bg-console`, `text-ink-3`, `rounded-frame`,
  `font-display`...), never raw hex, never `dark:` variants. A value you need that isn't a
  token: ask, don't invent one.
- Every island server-renders a useful final state: with no JavaScript and under reduced
  motion it shows the finished content, statically, and nothing depends on animation to be
  readable. Use `@steamfield/ui` (read `site/node_modules/@steamfield/ui/README.md` and its
  `.d.ts` files) for clocks, gating to on-screen, copy buttons and tabs rather than writing
  your own. Its playback gate already handles reduced motion and `[data-sf-motion="reduce"]`.
- Keyboard: every control is a real `<button>` or link, focus is visible (the global focus
  ring), and interactive demos announce state changes politely (`aria-live="polite"`) without
  re-announcing every streamed line.
- Phone widths (375px) work: no horizontal page scroll, long command lines scroll inside
  their own frame.
- Analytics: islands call `track()` from `src/lib/analytics.ts` with events declared in
  `src/lib/events.ts`; the names you need already exist.
- A sibling site built the same way, for reading only (never copy names or paths into tracked
  files): `~/Projects/rr/site/` (`src/components/landing/TerminalPlayer.tsx`,
  `CommandTabs.tsx`, `FlowDiagram.tsx`, `MonitorStage.tsx` and their tests show how islands
  there use `@steamfield/ui` and how they're tested).

## Goal

Build the "How a session runs" section's animated diagram (`docs/PRODUCT.md`; copy in
`src/data/landing.ts` `session`, already rendered as the section's title and lede). It shows
one realistic foreman session end to end: Claude Code managing three Codex delegates on
different models at once, the agents communicating through foreman, and most of foreman's
commands in use. It should be the most memorable visual on the page after the hero.

Model it on a proven pattern: read `~/Projects/rr/site/src/components/landing/FlowDiagram.tsx`
and `~/Projects/rr/site/src/lib/flow.ts` (and their tests) closely before designing.
Reuse the architecture, not the content: a pure timeline module that computes a `Scene` at
any time `t` plus an ordered step list; one SVG with a wide geometry (desktop) and a tall
geometry (phones) chosen by a media query; cubic links between ports with labeled packets
travelling along them; a synced step list under the diagram describing the current moment;
the `@steamfield/ui` playback clock (`usePlayback` from `@steamfield/ui/react/playback`)
gated to on-screen and reduced motion; a still frame for the server render, no-JS and
reduced motion; and a screen-reader summary paragraph describing the whole session.

### The cast (lanes)

Left: Claude Code (the orchestrator). Middle: the foreman daemon, drawn as a dispatch board
listing each run with its state square (run-state tokens), model and turn number, and a small
"held call" slot that lights in `signal` while a question is pending. Right: three delegate
cards, each a Codex agent in its own worktree, showing the run name, its branch
(`foreman/<name>`), a model chip, the current state, and a ticking count of commands and files
written. The delegates are the ones that built this page:

| Run | Model | Work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `site-console` | `gpt-6-astra` | design: the hero console |
| `site-commands` | `gpt-6.1-sol` | code: command tabs and llms.txt |
| `site-e2e` | `gpt-6.1-terra` | tests: browser and accessibility checks |

Model chips are neutral (ink on card), never colored by vendor. Name the models' roles in the
step text (astra for design taste, sol for implementation, terra for tests), not in marketing
language.

### The session (steps, in order)

Each step is a moment on the timeline with a title and a one- or two-sentence description in
the step list, and the packets, state changes and counters the diagram shows for it. Use the
command text exactly as foreman takes it (check the README's Commands table).

1. Claude writes three contracts (one per task, with its `May change` line).
2. `foreman start site-console --new-worktree --setup "bun install" --contract console.md --write --model gpt-6-astra`;
   the daemon creates `.claude/worktrees/site-console` on `foreman/site-console`, runs setup,
   starts a turn. Same for `site-commands` (sol) and `site-e2e` (terra), staggered.
3. Claude runs one `foreman wait --all` in the background and goes idle; the three delegates
   work, streaming events to the daemon (commands with ✓/✗, file writes).
4. `site-commands` calls `ask_orchestrator`: the daemon holds the tool call (held slot lights,
   state `waiting`), and Claude's wait returns `question` with id `q1`. The question text is
   the real recorded one: take it from `loadRun("site-commands")` (its first `Asked` record;
   the component receives it through `buildSession`). Show it truncated in the diagram and in
   full in the step list.
5. `foreman answer site-commands q1 "..."` with the recorded answer text (the matching
   `Resolved` record); the held call releases, `site-commands` returns to `running`, and the
   answer prints `next: foreman wait --all --after <cursor>`, which Claude runs.
6. `foreman steer site-e2e "Also check 375px widths."` while that turn is active and has no
   pending question (steer changes the active turn).
7. `site-console` finishes: wait returns `done` with its digest. Claude runs
   `foreman result site-console`, reviews the diff, runs the site's checks and commits.
8. `foreman followup site-console "Drop the false scope flags from the final step."` starts
   turn 2 on the same thread and worktree; it finishes quickly.
9. `site-commands` and `site-e2e` finish; Claude reviews and commits each.
10. `foreman archive` for all three: each worktree and branch is removed because its branch is
    merged; the cards empty out and the board shows them archived.

Timing: about 45 to 60 seconds of playback, with holds (about 2.5 seconds) at the question,
the answer, the steer, the first done and the archive. Packets are short labels on the links
(`start`, `turn`, `events`, `ask_orchestrator`, `question q1`, `answer`, `steer`, `done`,
`followup`, `archive`). Orange (`signal`) is only the question, the held call and the
`waiting` state, per DESIGN.md's rule about orange.

Still frame (server render, no JS, reduced motion): the moment after step 4, with `q1`
pending on `site-commands`, the other two running, and the held slot lit, plus the complete
step list as a static ordered list. Controls in a small bar above the diagram: Pause/Play,
Replay, and a step indicator ("Step 4 of 10"); selecting a step in the list jumps the clock to
it. Fire `demo_replayed {id: "session"}` on Replay.

Under the diagram, a one-line caption (already implied by the lede; keep it short and
written for the page) saying it's a simulation with compressed timings whose question and
answer text are recorded from `site-commands`.

## Interface

- `src/data/session.ts`: `buildSession(questionSource: Run): Session` (you design `Session`:
  delegates, steps, the recorded question and answer, timeline length) and the pure scene
  functions (`sceneAt(session, t)`, step lookup), all tested. No React.
- `src/components/landing/SessionDiagram.tsx`: `SessionDiagram({ session })`, rendered by
  `index.astro` as `<SessionDiagram client:visible session={buildSession(loadRun("site-commands"))} />`.
  Keep the export names and the prop. Subcomponents may go in
  `src/components/landing/session/`.

## Scope

- May change: `site/src/data/session.ts`, `site/src/data/session.test.ts`,
  `site/src/components/landing/SessionDiagram.tsx`,
  `site/src/components/landing/SessionDiagram.test.tsx`,
  `site/src/components/landing/session/`.
- Must not change: everything else, including `index.astro`, `primitives.tsx`, `global.css`,
  `landing.ts`, `runs.ts` and `fixtures/`. Request primitive, token or copy changes in the
  hand-off, or ask if blocked.
- Locked: none.

## Skills to apply

Find the newest installed Claude Code `claude-essentials` marketplace copy:

```sh
ce=$(ls -d "$HOME"/.claude/plugins/cache/*/ce/*/ | sort -V | tail -1)
```

Read the applicable skills; say in the hand-off where they changed your approach. The repo's
own rules win where they differ.

- `ce:writing-tests`: `${ce}skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md` for every test, including
  `references/waiting-typescript.md` for tests that wait on timers, and
  `references/flaky-tests.md` for isolation and repeat-run checks.
- `${ce}skills/design/SKILL.md` and `references/craft-tailwind.md`: craft rules for anything
  visual. `DESIGN.md` wins where they differ.
- `${ce}skills/architecting-systems/SKILL.md`: keep data shaping (pure, tested, in `src/data/`
  or `src/lib/`) separate from rendering.
- `${ce}skills/writer/SKILL.md`: any copy you write (captions, labels, empty states).

## Acceptance (every unit)

From `site/`, iterate until these pass:

```sh
bunx vitest run <your test files>
make lint
make check
make test
make build
```

Tests run in Vitest with happy-dom and Testing Library, through the component's real props
built from the real fixtures; drive time with fake timers or the library's test hooks, never
sleeps. Test the server-rendered final state (render to static markup) as well as the
interactive behaviour. Run each new test file three times on its own, then `make test` once.
Don't run `stacks verify` (the orchestrator does).

Then QA as the first user: run `make dev` (set `PORT_WEB` to a free port; `free-port 4400`
prints one), open the page with a real browser (Playwright from `node_modules` or the
`playwright-cli` skill if installed), and check your section at 1440px and 375px wide, with
motion on and with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and with JavaScript disabled. Save
screenshots to your review directory (below) and list them in the hand-off. Fix what looks
wrong against `DESIGN.md`. Stop the dev server when done.

## Do not

- Commit or push; leave changes for review.
- Disable lint, weaken a test, add a cast or suppress a type error to get green.
- Add features, options, abstractions or mechanisms the goal and acceptance do not need.
- Add a dependency; `@steamfield/ui`, React and Tailwind cover this.
- Edit `~/.codex` config, hooks, trust or auth.
- Mention any repository outside this one in a tracked file.

## Review before hand-off

Once acceptance checks pass, get one independent review in a fresh Codex process and resolve
its findings. Read `${ce}agents/code-reviewer.md`. There is no repo reviewer for `site/`.

Use separate simple commands and the file-writing tool, not a shell function, grouped command,
heredoc or generated shell script. Run from the worktree root:

```sh
mktemp -d
```

Keep the printed absolute directory as the review directory, outside the worktree. With the
file-writing tool, write `<review-directory>/prompt.md` containing, in this order:

1. The marketplace reviewer agent body without YAML frontmatter.
2. The applicable skill paths.
3. These task instructions and the full filled contract:

   "Review uncommitted changes and new files in {ABSOLUTE WORKTREE PATH} against base
   site/landing. Your sandbox is read-only; don't run tests or edit files. The author already
   ran the checks. Check the contract, site/DESIGN.md and site/AGENTS.md and report every real
   defect with a file:line reference."

Then run one plain command, replacing `{REVIEW DIR}` with that printed absolute path:

```sh
codex exec --ephemeral --sandbox read-only -m "gpt-6-astra" -c 'model_reasoning_effort="high"' -c 'service_tier="priority"' -o "{REVIEW DIR}/review.md" - < "{REVIEW DIR}/prompt.md"
```

Read the resulting `review.md`. Fix every finding or explain in the hand-off why it is wrong.
A bug finding gets a regression test before the fix. Rerun affected acceptance checks after
fixing. One independent review only. If the review cannot run, ask the orchestrator rather
than claiming it passed.

## Hand-off

Leave everything uncommitted and end with this report, naming files and symbols:

1. Summary: what you built, in two or three sentences.
2. Files: each file created or changed and why.
3. Decisions: choices left open, deviations and why, and where skills changed the approach.
4. Checks: each command and result with test counts; each new test file's three isolated runs
   and the full-suite result. QA: what you ran, the screenshot paths, what you changed.
5. Review: the review file's absolute path, each finding and its resolution or dispute.
6. Look closer at: assumptions, edge cases or tests the orchestrator should examine.
7. Open: unfinished work, blockers and questions.
